fields.v: Lu, P., Zhang, S., Hou, Y., Ye, L., Huang, C., Chen, Z., Zeng, J., Jiang, H., Liu, P., Wang, Y., Yang, M.-H. (2026). ProjDevBench: Benchmarking AI Coding Agents on End-to-End Project Development. arXiv:2602.01655v2 [cs.AI], 9 Feb 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2602.01655v2 [cs.AI] ('Preprint. February 10, 2026'); no venue stated

University of California, Merced (Lu, Wang, Yang); Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Lu, Zhang, Ye, Huang, Chen, Zeng, Jiang, Liu); Shanghai Innovation Institute (Lu, Liu); Beijing Institute of Technology (Hou)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — ProjDevBench benchmark (20 end-to-end project tasks, Online Judge testing plus rule-based and LLM-based code review) and evaluation of 6 coding agents with several LLM backends (16 agent-model configurations)

No SDD approach. Coding agents compared via CLI: Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Augment (Auggie CLI), Codex CLI, Gemini CLI (agent versions Not stated); models GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro Preview, GLM-4.6, Kimi-k2-0905-Preview, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp

N/A (no approach). Benchmark input per task: natural-language problem specification (README.md: functionality, input/output formats, constraints, submission requirements); partial codebase for project-completion (Easy) tasks; expected output a Git repository with multiple source files, CMakeLists.txt and executable

Standard agent prompt: 1. Analyze (read README.md), 2. Develop, 3. Git management (commit and push), 4. Submit to OJ (oj_client.py), 5. Iterate on errors within the submission limit, 6. Record (commit messages). Evaluation pipeline: OJ execution -> code review (rule-based + LLM) -> weighted final score
None (fully autonomous agents, no human feedback)
Full agent workflow (end-to-end project construction and iterative refinement), no specification approach
Not classifiable (agent benchmark; authors do not use SDD terms)
New project (project-creation, Hard: no initial codebase, 5 tasks) and existing partial codebase (project-completion, Easy: 15 tasks)

20 problems in 8 categories (from ~2,800 candidates, ~100 after scope filter); human reference solutions on average ~10 source files; human avg lines per problem 9.8-4,204.3, files 1-20 (Table 6); 2-18 submissions allowed per problem; agents averaged 138 turns and 4.81M tokens per problem, up to two hours

Undergraduate computer-science education Online Judge problems and course assignments: algorithms, data structures (STLite), management systems, interpreters (BASIC, Python, Scheme), storage (B+ tree), game, assembly (mov), optimization (GPU memory, buddy allocator)
N/A (autonomous agents, no participants). Human annotators for validating the LLM code review: number and profile Not stated ('domain experts' reformulated problem statements)

Interaction turns and token consumption per problem (aggregated over Claude Code with five models, Table 6); averages 138 turns and 4.81M tokens per problem; wall-clock time only as 'up to two hours'. No cost per configuration, no money

Execution Score (weighted share of passed OJ test cases, normalized 0-100; max over valid submissions); submission acceptance rate and verdict distribution (Accepted, Wrong Answer, Time/Memory Limit Exceeded, Runtime/Compile Error, Memory Leak); Final Score = 0.8 x Exec + 0.2 x Code Review

Code Review score (0-100): rule-based checks (forbidden patterns/headers, required or unchanged files, .gitignore, CMake output name) and LLM-as-a-judge readability and specification-compliance assessments
None

Failure-mode categories (specification misalignment, edge cases, time complexity, resource management, code engineering, version-control workflow); Spearman correlations of tokens, turns, net lines and file count with score; agreement of LLM review with humans (readability r = 0.709; binary rules accuracy 0.852, Cohen's kappa 0.710)

Automatic: OJ platform test execution and verdicts; Python rule-check scripts (checks.py, cr_list.json); LLM-as-a-judge (model Not stated); execution logs for tokens and turns; Docker container (Ubuntu 24.04, 8 GB, 4 CPU). Manual: failure-mode analysis; human annotators review a sample of submissions to validate the LLM review

Benchmark ProjDevBench, 20 problems, single pass each. Criterion: OJ test suites and code-review rules per task; no success criterion for a configuration stated by the authors. Overall Exec / CR / Final: (a) Augment + GPT-5: 72.13 / 73.26 / 72.35. (b) Augment + Sonnet-4.5: 66.06 / 86.28 / 70.10. (c) Codex CLI + GPT-5: 76.73 / 82.31 / 77.85 (Hard Exec 69.22). (d) Codex CLI + Sonnet-4.5: 57.52 / 71.98 / 60.41. (e) Gemini CLI + Gemini-3-Pro-Preview: 64.81 / 83.80 / 68.61 (Exec Easy 74.57 -> Hard 35.53). (f) Cursor + GPT-5: 69.26 / 82.23 / 71.85. (g) Cursor + Sonnet-4.5: 68.39 / 80.87 / 70.88. (h) Cursor + Gemini-3-Pro-Preview: 72.52 / 86.51 / 75.32. (i) GitHub Copilot + GPT-5: 58.64 / 74.06 / 61.73. (j) GitHub Copilot + Sonnet-4.5: 62.48 / 85.97 / 67.18 (Exec Easy 71.10 -> Hard 36.63). (k) GitHub Copilot + Gemini-3-Pro-Preview: 53.53 / 62.50 / 55.32. (l) Claude Code + DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp: 46.34 / 66.28 / 50.33. (m) Claude Code + GLM-4.6: 52.00 / 81.76 / 57.95. (n) Claude Code + GPT-5: 50.67 / 84.03 / 57.34. (o) Claude Code + Kimi-k2-0905-Preview: 49.00 / 67.83 / 52.77. (p) Claude Code + Sonnet-4.5: 63.76 / 89.31 / 68.87. For each: quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors (cost not reported per configuration)

Tasks: 20 ProjDevBench problems (15 Easy project-completion, 5 Hard project-creation). Configurations: 16 agent-model pairs (GPT-5 and Sonnet-4.5 on five agents, Gemini 3 Pro on Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, three open-source models on Claude Code). Baseline: none beyond the alternatives (student average scores given for reference only). Held constant: same prompts and problem specifications, Docker image, resource limits (8 GB, 4 CPU), per-problem submission limit (no fixed time budget); internet access allowed. Acceptance tests: OJ hidden test suites plus code review. Repetitions: single evaluation pass per configuration and problem. Human intervention: none

Codex + GPT-5 best (Final 77.85), then Cursor + Gemini-3-Pro (75.32), Augment + GPT-5 (72.35), Cursor + GPT-5 (71.85); lowest Claude Code + DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp (50.33). GPT-5 generally higher execution scores, Sonnet-4.5 higher code-review scores; Cursor and Augment stable across models (all > 70); open-source models below Sonnet-4.5 in Claude Code. Hard tasks: Codex + GPT-5 Exec 79.24 -> 69.22, Copilot + Sonnet 71.10 -> 36.63, Gemini CLI 74.57 -> 35.53. Only 27.38% of 1,768 submissions accepted (Wrong Answer 41.86%, TLE 13.91%). Tokens and turns negatively correlated with score (rho -0.734, p = 0.0002; -0.668, p = 0.0013). Significance: no tests in the main text; Appendix H states a paired t-test Cursor vs Claude Code p < 0.05 without details

Distinguished configurations (Final 50.33-77.85) and exposed failure modes not visible to tests (code review). Repeatability not assessed (single pass). LLM review validated against human annotators (kappa 0.710, accuracy 0.852). Limitations stated: only 20 tasks, mainly C++, fully autonomous agents only (no human-in-the-loop)

Only 20 tasks; scaling is hard because curating project-level problems with clear specifications and robust tests is costly; tasks mostly C++, generalization to other languages unclear; only fully autonomous agents, human-in-the-loop workflows excluded (future work). Gaps found: specification alignment, edge cases, time-complexity optimization, resource management, version-control workflow; agents fail to convert prolonged interaction into progress

Inconsistencies: p. 5 says the three open-source models score '52.77, 50.33, and 57.95 respectively' after listing GLM-4.6, Kimi, DeepSeek, while Table 2 and the next sentence give GLM 57.95, Kimi 52.77, DeepSeek 50.33 (Table 2 used). Appendix H (p. 16) gives mean 54.16, 'problem complexity vs score r = -0.72', 'code review vs OJ r = 0.68' and a Cursor vs Claude Code t-test, none derived in the main text and not matching Table 4 (Spearman); the 'top agents' named there are not the top configurations in Table 2. The abstract's 'overall acceptance rate 27.38%' is the share of all submissions accepted (Table 3), not a task resolve rate. Tokens/turns in Table 6 only for Claude Code. LLM judge model and number of human annotators Not stated. Table 2 layout scrambled in the text; Claude Code rows rebuilt from the column order and checked against Final = 0.8 Exec + 0.2 CR. Benchmark public: https://github.com/zsworld6/projdevbench. No pre-registration. Programming language: C++ (also mov assembly)

rev.why: Single evaluation pass per configuration (p. 5), so no repetitions; the only difference test is a paired t-test claimed in Appendix H without details and not matching the main text. Spearman correlations concern tasks, not configuration differences. Partly vs No is a judgement call.
